idea: VocacionData AI: Vocational guidance based on real labor data for Peruvian applicants and students, using a conversational agent that crosses interests, salaries, employability, university offerings, and location to reduce poor career decisions.
market: Peruvian postulants and students facing a critical career choice with limited data-driven guidance; TAM of ~500k annual school graduates and ~1.2M university students, with high information asymmetry.

solutions.name: Portal MiFuturo (Pronabec/MINEDU)
solutions.observed_positioning: Free official source of university programs, tuition, and labor outcomes.

solutions.name: Ponte en Carrera (MTPE)
solutions.observed_positioning: Salary and employability statistics per career, renewed annually by labor survey.

solutions.name: LinkedIn Salary Insights
solutions.observed_positioning: Global platform with localized salary data from self-reported profiles, limited to professional roles.

solutions.name: ChatGPT / OpenAI
solutions.observed_positioning: Conversational agent that can provide career advice based on broad web knowledge, not tailored to local data.

solutions.name: Career Counselors (private + school staff)
solutions.observed_positioning: One-on-one guidance often based on psychometric tests and personal experience; low scalability.

solutions.name: Test de Holland (RIASEC) online
solutions.observed_positioning: Free/paid web tests matching personality to broad career families, without local labor context.

solutions.name: University Career Fairs & Open Houses
solutions.observed_positioning: Direct exposure to programs and alumni, but time‑intensive and institution‑biased.

solutions.name: YouTube / TikTok career influencers
solutions.observed_positioning: Unstructured peer advice and day‑in‑the‑life content, trending among Gen Z.

solutions.name: Manual research on university websites
solutions.observed_positioning: Prospective students browse curricula, brochures, and scattered job forums on their own.

solutions.name: Family & peer pressure
solutions.observed_positioning: Choices heavily influenced by parental expectations or friend trends, ignoring labor data.

solutions.name: Bumeran / CompuTrabajo job listings
solutions.observed_positioning: Reveals demand and advertised salaries for specific roles; no comparative tool for careers.

solutions.name: Glassdoor / Indeed Peru
solutions.observed_positioning: Salary brackets and employee reviews for companies, not career‑entry guidance.

solutions.name: Coursera / EdX Career Academy
solutions.observed_positioning: Skill‑based career paths and certificates, weak on Peruvian university system mapping.

solutions.name: Laboratoria (Peruvian bootcamp)
solutions.observed_positioning: Targets women for digital skills, with employment outcomes, but only for tech roles.

solutions.name: Apps like ‘Elegir Carrera’ (Universia)
solutions.observed_positioning: Basic test+name‑match, rarely updated with current salaries or regional demand.

research_summary: Identified 15 alternatives spanning government data portals, global platforms, legacy psychometrics, human counselors, social media, and DIY methods. The five most dangerous competitors were selected based on their data depth, user reach, and potential to block adoption of a new AI native tool.

competitor_signals.sourcing_brief: Government portal with institutional traffic; low innovation capacity but high trust and free access.
MTPE´s salary observatory; updated yearly with official INEI data, but static and slow to iterate.
Global network effects, potential to add AI‑career guidance features for Peru; strong data on professional salaries but weak on entry‑level and university match.
Rapid AI evolution could obsolete vertical solutions if it integrates hyper‑local labor data; current responses lack Peru‑specific accuracy.
Fragmented and labor‑intensive; high trust in personal contact but no real‑time data integration.
